Its one-component wildcard matches the inherent impl segment instead; exact method suffixes select both ReserveData conversions and live Reserve wrappers. This is a documented selector limitation, not evidence that source extraction failed. --start-from (not --start-from-if-exists) requires actual matches; generated declarations and source spans still require inspection.
source_boundary.configuration: --locked --release --lib --no-default-features; no cfg(kani), test, testutils or certora; production release overflow-checks=true retained.

commands.prerequisites: Python >=3.11, existing rustup launcher in PATH, systemd user manager enforcing the listed limits, downloaded hash-pinned sandbox tools and usable pinned compiler. Compiler identity is checked before Charon, CHARON_TOOLCHAIN_IS_IN_PATH=1 disables its fallback installer, and RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL=0 disables rustup proxy installation. Cargo may fetch exact Cargo.lock dependencies into the sandbox cargo-home.
commands.bounds: Driver reuses scripts/verify_local.py::contained and its shared serialization lock: actual cgroup-v2 limit checks, 4 GiB memory, zero swap, 256 tasks, CPU at most 200%, OOM group killing, whole-unit cleanup and a 600-second deadline. No uncontained fallback.
commands.artifacts: Each new output directory contains command.log and invocation.json with exact argv, compiler identity, tool hashes, source hashes before/after, generated hashes and dependency source hashes. Charon emits pool.llbc. Aeneas requires the matching successful/current-source Charon receipt, checks LLBC target information, inherits that target unless explicitly matched, and consumes a hashed immutable input snapshot. It emits Lean definitions plus unproved external templates. Existing output directories and stale/conflicting receipts are rejected.
commands.flags_justification: Installed help and the first real runs justify the selected flags. Charon's --preset=aeneas, --start-from, --include, --opaque, --sysroot=default, --dest-file and --error-on-warnings are retained. Aeneas uses -backend lean, -split-files, -warnings-as-errors, -sequential and -dest. Its supported -print-unknown-externals reporting flag crashed on tuple names and was removed; no source algorithm, borrow/type check or target semantic check was disabled.
commands.lean_checking: Not automated by this feasibility driver: first inspect actual generated external templates and signatures. Build a Lean package with the bundled lean-toolchain and require aeneas from the exact sandbox tools/backends/lean path, preserving its lake-manifest pins. Restore/compile dependency caches and run lake build only under the same parent containment policy. Unimplemented external templates are a stop outcome; do not fill them with sorry, axioms, admits or copied target financial implementations.

unclosed_obligations: Extraction and translation succeeded at this exact pinned seam; no arithmetic/source-refinement theorem was proved.
Generated external templates are unproved obligations, not permission to introduce target axioms or trusted stubs. No Lean theorem was checked against them.

SDK Env and I256 signatures/wrappers remain opaque. To refine them inspect SDK num.rs:345-396,399-435 and the shared numeric comparison implementation: exact byte sign-extension/round-trip, from_i32/from_i128, to_i128 representability, obj_cmp, i256_mul/div/rem_euclid/add/sub, byte construction/append/slice/read and conversion all require host/SDK contracts or further source-connected proofs.

For both signs, prove checked i128 multiplication selection, truncating division plus Euclidean-remainder adjustment, exact/inexact quotient, denominator zero rejection, i128::MIN / -1 rejection and representability. Do not assume the product fits i128 merely because the result does.

The concrete MAX*2/(MAX-1) production fixture ran through math::tests::rounding_keeps_i256_fallback and passed (floor=2, ceil=3). This is smoke evidence, not a universal bridge. Denominator-zero and unrepresentable-result cases were not exercised by this campaign.

Default distributed sysroot lacks some standard-library MIR. Missing bodies must remain visible, justified by existing checked backend models or separately extracted; no missing-body diagnostic was observed yet.

Aeneas --help states drops are not evaluated by default. Any drop, allocation, panic/unwind or unsafe behavior relevant to Env/host state needs an explicit semantic argument or a separately recorded supported extraction configuration. Charon's Aeneas preset performs its documented lowering passes; compiler/Charon/Aeneas correctness remains trusted.
Host transaction atomicity, accepted-call overflow/rejection behavior and no committed mutation on traps remain explicit separate premises, not a conclusion of source extraction.
Lean runtime is installed; package caches/Aeneas olean restoration and Lean checking were not run. Generated definitions exist, but the external-model and arithmetic proof obligations remain open.

No production source, runtime dependency, ABI, storage, rounding or user-owned docs/verification-design.md was modified. No hosted proof was submitted. Campaign commits and the authorized branch push are tracked separately; no PR or deployment is part of this work.
stop_policy: Retain exact command.log, invocation.json, compiler/extractor diagnostic and generated partial artifacts on compilation failure, unmatched selectors, missing body/model, unsupported construct, timeout, OOM or translation failure. Do not infer source incompatibility from a tool download/setup failure. Do not replace target bodies with handwritten models, narrow numeric domains, trust external templates or increase the timeout to manufacture a pass. Creusot/Why3 has not been installed or proposed as an automatic migration: evaluate it against this same exact seam only after an actual extraction blocker has been recorded.
